subject: MSA & Order Form: DPA — processor delegation, SCCs and transfer evidence
messages:
From: Elena Vasiliev <elena@cardiocloud.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brookes <tom.brookes@cardiocloud.com>, CardioCloud Legal <legal@cardiocloud.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA redlines and processor roles — initial questions

Hi Monica,

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA and order form last week. Our legal team reviewed the attached DPA redline and had a few open items we need clarified before we can proceed to procurement: 

- Processor/processor-subprocessor roles: the redline as written assumes CardioCloud is a controller for end-user PII; our privacy team thinks there are parts of the workflow where Redwood will be acting as a joint-controller (mainly around telemetry used for model improvement). Can you confirm Redwood's stance?
- SCCs: CardioCloud needs confirmation that Redwood will execute the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (Annex A) and provide a signed annex.
- Transfer Impact Assessment: please share the most recent TIA and any mitigations for transfers outside the EEA (e.g., data residency, contractual safeguards).

I've attached our redlined DPA for reference. Can we get a short call this week so our teams can align? Proposed times: Thu 30 Sep 09:00-11:00 CEST or Fri 01 Oct 14:00-16:00 CEST.

Regards,
Elena Vasiliev
Head of Privacy & Compliance
CardioCloud
Attachments: CardioCloud_DPA_Redline_v2.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasiliev <elena@cardiocloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and processor roles — initial questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the redline. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps: 

- Redwood position on roles: our default is that for customer prompts and outputs we act as processor; however, telemetry collected for model ops (aggregated logs + non-identifiable prompts used for safety) may be processed under a different lawful basis. We can accept a joint-controller clause limited to telemetry if CardioCloud requires it, but we need scoping language.
- SCCs: yes, we will execute the SCCs and sign an annex — I will attach the standard Annex A template and flag the signed copy to legal once routed.
- TIA: attaching our latest transfer-impact-assessment and mitigation summary.

Next steps: looping in Laura (privacy counsel) and Karthik (contracts) to propose specific redline language for controller/processor delegation and an evidence checklist for transfers. Laura/Karthik, can you review CardioCloud's redline and suggest wording by Thu EOD so we can offer a consolidated response and proposed small-scope call?

Available for the call Thu 30 Sep 09:30 CEST if that works for you.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SCCs_Annex_A.pdf, transfer-impact-assessment.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: RE: DPA redlines and processor roles — proposed edits

Monica/Laura — I reviewed CardioCloud's redline overnight. High-level recommendations: 

1) Controller/Processor: propose a narrowly scoped joint-controller clause limited to aggregated telemetry used for model monitoring/improvement (defined in a new Exhibit B). We'll explicitly exclude prompt content and generated outputs.
2) Subprocessor flowdowns: CardioCloud wants audit-level evidence (SOC 2 + processor listing). We can provide SOC 2 and a list of active subprocessors, but push back on ad-hoc audit access; offer a regular cadence (quarterly) and a SOC 2 bridge letter instead.
3) SCCs Annex: we should attach our standard SCCs Annex as-is; flag one non-negotiable: Redwood cannot accept open-ended obligations to re-engineer model behavior to suit controller preferences.

I'll draft the exact language for Sections 2.1-2.4 of the DPA and attach in the next email. Rishi — heads up this may add a slight execution delay (2-3 business days) if CardioCloud insists on additional evidence.

-Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasiliev <elena@cardiocloud.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: RE: DPA redlines and processor roles — privacy counsel notes

Hi Elena — thanks for the redline. A few privacy-counsel level points and proposed clean language below. Apologies for the long note; I wanted to be explicit so procurement has workable text.

- Proposed telemetry carve-out (new Exhibit B): "Telemetry" defined as aggregate, de-identified logs used strictly for service reliability, safety and model monitoring. Redwood will not use Telemetry for profiling or for deriving individualized product recommendations unless CardioCloud provides prior opt-in.

- Scope of processing: Replace CardioCloud's 'Controller' assertion with a clause identifying customer data categories (prompts, attachments, outputs, account metadata). For prompts/outputs, Redwood acts as processor. For telemetry, Redwood is a joint-controller solely for defined processing purposes.

- Transfers & Mitigations: See attached TIA. Where transfers occur to countries without an adequacy decision, we rely on SCCs + encryption in transit + contractual logging. We can propose a limited subprocessor list and consent window.

- Evidence: Offer 1) current SOC 2 report (for review under NDA), 2) subprocessor register, and 3) the TIA workbook. We will not permit continuous on-site audits; propose a 30-day remediation and a 3rd-party spot-check mechanism instead.

Suggested path: Monica sends consolidated DPA redline incorporating the telemetry carve-out + SCC annex; CardioCloud returns with any remaining redlines within 3 business days. If still outstanding, schedule an escalation call with Legal (max 30 minutes).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Brookes <tom.brookes@cardiocloud.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Vasiliev <elena@cardiocloud.com>, CardioCloud Legal <legal@cardiocloud.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 14:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and processor roles — follow-up and evidence request

Monica/Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications before we lock the call: 

- Telemetry carve-out: CardioCloud can accept a tight telemetry definition limited to aggregated, non-identifiable logs. We need explicit language preventing re-identification and a commitment to retention limits (90 days for telemetry by default).
- Evidence: please upload the SOC 2 package and subprocessor register to the drive link you shared (we have an NDA in place). If possible, include a brief note per subprocessor on location of processing.
- SCCs: we'll review the Annex A template; can you confirm Redwood will complete and countersign the SCCs before order execution?

If you can upload the SOC 2 and subprocessor register by EOD Mon 04 Oct we'll be ready to finalize. If not, we will need to move decision to our procurement lead and potentially delay the pilot start.

Thanks — Tom
